Diffuse Textures
The default usual texture dimensions are the following:
– 1024x1024x32bit
– 1024x1024x32bit. As required up to 2048
– 2048x2048x24bit (no alpha). As required up to 2048

The endings are added to the files of textures:
«_c» postfix is for textures without alpha channel
«_a» postfix is for textures with alpha channel
Important!
f3f_1_cockpit_body.psd
f3f_1_cockpit_gauges.psd etc.
Normal and Specular Textures
Min Z = 0, Scale = 8.
The normal map Y (green) channel must NOT be inverted.
Normals and Y (green) channel
Primary surfaces (paintwork): K~80-90% (40-70 RGB)
Bare metal (chips, wear) K~20-40% (170-210 RGB)
Materials (the order of material IDs)
(1) – glass
(2) – body
(3) – gauges
(4) – gauges_dmg (damaged instrument glass)
(5) – collimator or sight
(6) – collimator_glass or sight_glass (for gunsight glass)
(7) – bullet_glass* (canopy glass holes)
(8) – bullet_metal* (holes in the hull)
(9) – labels (optional)
(10) – boxes (optional)
(11) – flare_red** (red lamp flare)
(12) – flare_green** (green lamp flare)

glass_a_dmg

LOD2 – 200 to 550 meters
LOD3 – 550+ meters
Aircraft model positioning
Draw 50% chord line (divides tip and root chord in half)
Extend tip and root chords with opposite copies
Draw a line connecting resulting extremes

Destruction credit mechanics
Aircraft
Instant destruction
Damaged
Conditions of target destruction
Critical damage
Activity timer:
90 seconds (then becomes the lowest priority).
Conditions required when assigning to the target:
Features:
Serious damage
30/60/80 seconds (AB/RB/SB) (reset at end of timer).
Simple damage
AB 12 seconds / RB & SB 15 seconds(reset at end of timer).
Crash reward
Conditions for target destruction
Active fire
no timer.
Conditions required when assigning to a target:
disabling a crew member, weapon, engine or transmission.
30/60/80 (AB/RB/SB) seconds (reset after timer end).
12/15/15 (AB/RB/SB) seconds (reset after end of timer).
Any hits causing damage.
The greatest award will be credited for caused damage.
There are no crew left in “black” (destroyed) compartments.

Air Combat — Kfir 101
managing energy, positioning, and knowing when to engage.
Sideclimbing and then diving on the enemy team + hit n' run
On the runway, turn the radar off.
The enemy team should now be on your direct right
as the element of surprise is crucial here.
Deploy the airbrakes to slow down if needed.
Prioritize enemies that are the closest/slowest/distracted.
Maintain your energy until you need to use it.
Base bombing
Also, bring along the two AIM-9Gs and a drop tank.
DO NOT TUNNEL VISION.
Never dogfight with a payload.
You will not be able to drop the bombs at higher speeds.
General tips to be successful in the Kfir Canard
Rely on your flight performance and not your missiles.

Creating more advanced objectgroups
Airfields
Code for adding airfields
start: Starting position of the runway
start:p3=835.0, 0.0, 40.0
end: Ending position of the runway
end:p3=-835.0, 0.0, 40.0
width: Total width of the airfield
width:r=140.0
spawn: Spawn position(s) (in metres)
Meaning of numbers in start, end and spawn lines:
First number — X axis, the north/south position
Second number — Y axis, height (Does not need to be used)
Third number — Z axis, the east/west position

Strela-10
The hull used for the Strela-10 is based on the
multi-purpose towing lightly armoured vehicle”
(MT-LB) chassis
The Strela-10 is powered by a
YaMZ-238 V8 diesel
The transporter-erector launcher and radar (TELAR)

9S86 “Snap Shot” pulse Doppler
9S16 “Flat Box-B” passive radar detection system
360º Azov L-136 MAK-F IRST
to search for infrared sources.
The 9K35M4 Strela-10 features a thermal/optical two-channel
electro-optical block (EOB)
TAM-150 6×6 truck
. This allows the vehicle to reach speeds of 90 km/h.
